issues.legal_issue: The effect of a decree on heirs who were not impleaded in a creditor’s action against heirs of a deceased debtor is governed by procedural law rather than the deceased’s personal law.
material_facts: The creditor brought an action to enforce a mortgage after the debtor had died, impleading some, but not all, of the deceased’s heirs.
The omitted heir argued that under Muslim personal law the decree could affect only the interests of the heirs who had been impleaded.
issues.conclusion: Whether the decree bound the entire estate or only the impleaded heirs was a question of procedure, not one determined by the deceased’s personal law.
issues.legal_principle: Although the judgment recognised that under Muslim law an estate devolves on the heirs at death and each heir’s liability for the deceased’s debts is proportionate to that heir’s share, the effect of a decree on absent heirs is governed by procedural law. The Court applied the principle in Daya Ram v. Shyam Sundari, which it held applicable irrespective of community. It considered the argument based on Order 22 rules 4 and 5 and section 2(11) of the Code of Civil Procedure, but did not make the applicability of the principle depend on heirs being added to a pending suit under those provisions.

predicates.creditor_suit_for_deceased_debt: A creditor brought a suit to recover a debt from the estate of a debtor who had died.
predicates.omitted_heir_challenges_decree_scope_und: An heir who was not impleaded contended that the deceased’s personal law limited the decree’s effect to the interests of the heirs who were impleaded.

issues.definition: When a creditor brings a suit to recover a deceased debtor’s debt and an omitted heir challenges the decree’s scope under personal law, the decree’s binding effect is determined by procedural law.

issues.legal_issue: Heirs impleaded after a diligent and bona fide inquiry may represent the entire estate in a creditor’s action against heirs of a deceased debtor, subject to the absence of fraud, collusion, an unfair trial, or an untried special defence of an absent heir.
material_facts: After the debtor died, the creditor brought a mortgage-enforcement action against some of the heirs, but did not implead the plaintiff or his brother.
The courts found that the creditor had made a bona fide inquiry and genuinely believed that the impleaded widows and daughter were the only heirs, and that they were in possession of the estate.
The omitted heirs were minors when the mortgage action was brought.
The plaintiff did not claim a special defence that could have been raised in the earlier action, and the Court found no basis to conclude that there had not been a fair or real trial.
issues.conclusion: The omitted heirs were sufficiently represented, and the decree bound the entire estate.
issues.legal_principle: Where a creditor, after diligent and bona fide inquiry, impleads persons in the genuine belief that they are the only persons interested in the deceased’s estate, those persons may represent the entire estate and the decree may bind heirs not impleaded. The rule derives from Daya Ram v. Shyam Sundari and applies irrespective of personal law. It does not apply where there is fraud or collusion, circumstances showing that the trial was not fair or real, or a special defence of an absent heir that was not and could not be tried in the earlier proceeding.

predicates.creditor_suit_against_deceased_debtor_he: A creditor brought a suit against some heirs to recover a debt owed by a deceased debtor.
predicates.diligent_bona_fide_inquiry: The creditor made a diligent and bona fide inquiry to identify the persons interested in the estate.
predicates.genuine_belief_only_interested_persons: The creditor genuinely believed that the persons impleaded were the only persons interested in the estate.
predicates.fraud_or_collusion: The creditor and an impleaded heir acted fraudulently or in collusion in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.unfair_or_unreal_trial: Circumstances in the earlier proceeding showed that there was not a fair or real trial.
predicates.absent_heir_untried_special_defense: An absent heir had a special defence that was not and could not be tried in the earlier proceeding.

issues.definition: When a creditor sues some heirs over a deceased debtor’s debt, the impleaded heirs may represent the entire estate if the creditor made a diligent and bona fide inquiry and genuinely believed they were the only interested persons, unless there was fraud or collusion, an unfair or unreal trial, or an untried special defence of an absent heir; in that event the decree binds the entire estate.
